sectionOne.heading: Experience first.
body: Experiential and inquiry-based learning is the school's stated approach rather than an enrichment attached to it: a topic is met in the hand before it is met in the exam. The **twelve laboratories** are what make that possible in an ordinary week rather than on a special day.

The school's own account of a Gallery Walk puts it plainly — children *“confidently presented their projects, charts, and models, turning the classroom into a mini exhibition hall.”* The work came first; the explaining came after it.

steps.body: A material, a tool, a problem that has not been explained yet.

steps.label: Question
steps.body: The school calls it “sparking curiosity, scientific thinking” — the moment a child wants to know why.
steps.photoAlt: A young student of {schoolName} holding a hand-made rocket cut-out at the Star Gazing session, the night sky on the board behind

steps.label: Discover
steps.body: The answer arrives having been looked for. That is what makes it stay.
steps.photoAlt: Children of {schoolName} sitting in a ring inside the Taramandal planetarium dome, faces turned upward

sectionThree.heading: Not a special day.
body: A planting plot, a planetarium and a telescope are not the decoration around the curriculum — they are where parts of it are taught. The school's record of the stargazing evening is that the campus *“transformed into a window to the universe.”*

close.quote: Twelve laboratories, a planting plot and a night sky — so that what a child learns has been handled before it is answered.
